questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT a part of the classical cell theory?
options_en: All living organisms are composed of cells.
Cells arise only from pre-existing cells.
Cells are the basic units of life.
questions.solution_en:
• The classical cell theory does not mention the presence of a nucleus in all cells.

• Prokaryotic cells, which are also a type of cell and present in bacteria, do not have a well-defined nucleus.

Further Insight:

• Cell Theory

○ Developed through contributions by Matthias Schleiden, Theodor Schwann, and Rudolf Virchow, the Cell Theory is a fundamental concept in biology that defines the properties of cells.

○ Key Points of Cell Theory:

■ All living organisms are composed of cells: Schleiden and Schwann proposed that both plant and animal tissues are made of cells.

■ Cells are the basic unit of life: They form the foundation of biological structure and function.

■ Cells arise only from pre-existing cells: Virchow added this crucial concept, stating "Omnis cellula e cellula" (All cells come from cells), which confirmed that cells reproduce by dividing.

questions.q_en: Which scientist is incorrectly matched with his contribution to cell theory?
options_en: Rudolf Virchow - Proposed that cells arise from pre-existing cells.
questions.solution_en:
○ The nucleus was discovered by Robert Brown, not Theodor Schwann. Schwann, along with Schleiden, proposed that all animals and plants are made of cells.

○ Robert Hooke coined the term "cell,".

○ Leeuwenhoek observed living cells.

○ Virchow proposed "Omnis cellula e cellula."

Further Insight:

• Cell Theory

• The Cell Theory was developed by three scientists and provides the foundation for modern biology.

○ Matthias Schleiden (1838): Studied plants and concluded that all plant tissues are made of cells.

○ Theodor Schwann (1839): Extended Schleiden's theory to animals, concluding that all animals are also made of cells.

○ Rudolf Virchow (1855): Expanded the theory by introducing the idea that cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula e cellula).

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements correctly describes features of plant cells?

a. Plant cells contain a cell wall made of chitin.

b. Plastids, such as chloroplasts, are found only in plant cells.

c. Plant cells typically have large central vacuoles.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Plant cell wall is made of cellulose, not chitin (which is found in fungi).

• Plastids, including chloroplasts, are unique to plant cells.

• Plant cells generally have large central vacuoles for storage and maintaining turgidity.

Further Insight:

• Plant Cell:

• Type: Eukaryotic cell, found in plants.

• Cell Wall: Present; made of cellulose, providing structural strength.

• Key Organelles:

○ Nucleus: Contains genetic material (DNA).

○ Mitochondria: Produces energy (ATP).

○ Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER): Involved in protein and lipid synthesis.

○ Golgi Apparatus: Packaging and transportation of proteins.

○ Chloroplasts: Enable photosynthesis (conversion of light energy into chemical energy).

○ Large Central Vacuole: Maintains turgor pressure and stores nutrients.

• Other Features: Contains plasmodesmata (channels for communication between cells).

questions.q_en: Which of the following is TRUE for both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
questions.solution_en:
• Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells contain ribosomes for protein synthesis.

• Prokaryotes, however, do not have membrane-bound organelles, their DNA is not enclosed in a nucleus , and they typically have circular chromosomes

Further Insight:

• Types of Cells

○ Cells are broadly classified into two types based on the presence of a nucleus and organelles:

○ Prokaryotic Cells:

■ Found in organisms like bacteria and cyanobacteria (blue-green algae).

■ Characteristics:

• Lack a well-defined nucleus; instead, have a nucleoid region where DNA is concentrated.

• Lack membrane-bound organelles.

• Smaller (typically 0.5-5 µm in size) and reproduce by binary fission.

• Structures include cell wall, plasma membrane, ribosomes, and mesosomes (for cellular respiration).

■ Example: E. coli, Mycoplasma (smallest living cells).

○ Eukaryotic Cells:

■ Found in plants, animals, fungi, and protists.

■ Characteristics:

• Contain a well-defined nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

• Possess membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and endoplasmic reticulum.

• Larger and more complex than prokaryotic cells.

■ Examples: Plant cells, Animal cells, Fungi.

•

questions.q_en: Which of the following organelles is involved in both protein synthesis and transport within the cell?
questions.solution_en:
• The RER is involved in protein synthesis (via ribosomes) and the transport of proteins synthesized on its surface.

Further Insight:

• The Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) is a network of membranous tubules and flattened sacs found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells. It plays a vital role in the synthesis, folding, modification, and transport of proteins and lipids.

○ Types of Endoplasmic Reticulum:

○ Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER):

■ It has ribosomes attached to its surface, giving it a "rough" appearance.

■ Primarily involved in the synthesis of proteins, especially those to be exported out of the cell or inserted into the cell membrane. Proteins synthesized here are also transported to the Golgi apparatus for further modification.

○ Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER):

■ Lacks ribosomes, giving it a "smooth" appearance.

■ Involved in the synthesis of lipids, including phospholipids and steroids. It also detoxifies harmful metabolic byproducts and stores calcium ions in muscle cells (important for muscle contraction).

•

questions.q_en: Which of the following events occurs during mitosis but NOT during meiosis?
options_en: Reduction of chromosome number by half.
questions.solution_en:
• Mitosis results in the formation of two genetically identical daughter cells, while meiosis results in four genetically distinct haploid cells.

Further Insight:

• Mitosis

○ Mitosis is a type of cell division that results in two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

○ Mitosis consists of four main stages:

■ Prophase: Chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes; the nuclear envelope begins to break down.

■ Metaphase: Chromosomes align at the cell's equatorial plane.

■ Anaphase: Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles of the cell.

■ Telophase: Nuclear membranes reform around each set of chromosomes, and the cell prepares to divide.

■ Mitosis is essential for growth, development, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction in organisms.

○ Chromosome Number: The chromosome number remains diploid (2n) in the daughter cells, identical to the parent cell.

• Meiosis

○ Meiosis is a specialized type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four genetically diverse daughter cells (gametes).

○ Meiosis consists of two sequential divisions: Meiosis I and Meiosis II, each with its own stages.

■ Meiosis I:

• Prophase I: Homologous chromosomes pair up and exchange genetic material (crossing over).

• Metaphase I: Paired chromosomes align at the equator.

• Anaphase I: Homologous chromosomes are separated to opposite poles.

• Telophase I: Two new nuclei form, leading to two haploid (n) cells.

■ Meiosis II: Similar to mitosis, where sister chromatids are separated, resulting in four haploid cells.

○ Meiosis is crucial for sexual reproduction, producing gametes (sperm and eggs) that carry genetic diversity.

○ The chromosome number is halved, resulting in haploid (n) cells, which is essential for maintaining the species' chromosome number upon fertilization.

•

• (image source: Times of India)

questions.q_en: Which of the following is TRUE regarding the Golgi apparatus?
options_en: It is the site of cellular respiration.
It modifies, sorts, and packages proteins.
questions.solution_en:
• The Golgi apparatus is responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other parts of the cell.

Further Insight:

• Golgi apparatus

○ The Golgi apparatus, also known as the Golgi complex or Golgi body, is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells. It is primarily involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.

○ Structure:

■ Composed of a series of flattened, stacked pouches called cisternae.

■ Has a distinct polarity with a cis face (receiving side) oriented towards the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and a trans face (shipping side) oriented towards the cell membrane.

○ Functions:

■ Protein Modification: Modifies proteins synthesized in the rough ER by adding carbohydrate (glycosylation) or phosphate groups (phosphorylation).

■ Sorting and Packaging: Packages proteins into vesicles for transport to their final destinations, including secretion outside the cell, delivery to lysosomes, or incorporation into the cell membrane.

■ Lipid Metabolism: Involved in the modification and transport of lipids, including the synthesis of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

○ Significance:

■ Essential for proper cell function as it processes and directs proteins and lipids critical for cellular activities.

■ Plays a role in the formation of lysosomes, which are vital for digestion and waste removal in cells.

•

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements about ribosomes is/are correct?

a. Ribosomes are responsible for protein synthesis in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

b. They are membrane-bound organelles attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells.

c. Ribosomes consist of RNA and proteins.

Select the correct answer:
questions.solution_en:
○ Ribosomes synthesize proteins in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

○ Ribosomes themselves are not membrane-bound organelles; they can be free-floating in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough ER.

○ Ribosomes are made of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.

Further Insight:

•

• Ribosomes

• Ribosomes are small, spherical structures found in all living cells, responsible for protein synthesis.

○ Structure:

■ Composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.

■ Consist of two subunits: a large subunit and a small subunit, which come together during protein synthesis.

■ 70S Ribosomes in Prokaryotes, and 80S Ribosomes in Eukaryotes

○ Types:

■ Free Ribosomes: Float freely in the cytoplasm, synthesizing proteins that function within the cytosol.

■ Bound Ribosomes: Attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (rough ER), synthesizing proteins destined for secretion or for use in membranes.

○ Function:

■ Protein Synthesis: Translate messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences into polypeptide chains, which fold into functional proteins.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is a unique feature of plant cells?
questions.solution_en:
• The cell wall is a structure unique to plant cells, providing rigidity and protection.

• Mitochondria produce energy, ribosomes are present in both plant and animal cells. Mitochondria produce energy, ribosomes synthesize proteins, and the plasma membrane surrounds the cell in both cell types.

Further Insight:

• Plant Cell:

• Type: Eukaryotic cell, found in plants.

• Cell Wall: Present; made of cellulose, providing structural strength.

• Key Organelles:

○ Nucleus: Contains genetic material (DNA).

○ Mitochondria: Produces energy (ATP).

○ Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER): Involved in protein and lipid synthesis.

○ Golgi Apparatus: Packaging and transportation of proteins.

○ Chloroplasts: Enable photosynthesis (conversion of light energy into chemical energy).

○ Large Central Vacuole: Maintains turgor pressure and stores nutrients.

• Other Features: Contains plasmodesmata (channels for communication between cells).

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements about animal cells is FALSE?
options_en: Animal cells lack a cell wall.
Animal cells store energy in the form of starch.
questions.solution_en:
• Animal cells store energy primarily as glycogen, not starch. Starch is the energy storage form in plants.

• Animal cells contain centrioles involved in cell division.

• Animal cells lack a cell wall and contain lysosomes for waste digestion.

Further Insight:

• Animal Cell:

○ Type: Eukaryotic cell, found in multicellular organisms.

○ Cell Wall: Absent; has a flexible plasma membrane.

○ Key Organelles:

■ Nucleus: Contains genetic material (DNA).

■ Mitochondria: Produces energy (ATP).

■ Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER): Involved in protein and lipid synthesis.

■ Golgi Apparatus: Packaging and transportation of proteins.

■ Lysosomes: Responsible for digestion and waste removal.

○ Special Structures:

■ Centrioles: Play a role in cell division.

○ Other Features: Lacks chloroplasts and a large central vacuoles

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT a difference between plant and animal cells?
options_en: Plant cells contain chloroplasts, while animal cells do not.
Plant cells have large central vacuoles, while animal cells have small, temporary vacuoles.
Plant cells contain centrioles, while animal cells do not.
Plant cells have a rigid cell wall, while animal cells lack a cell wall.
questions.solution_en:
• Centrioles are typically found in animal cells and are absent in most plant cells.

• Chloroplasts are unique to plant cells for photosynthesis.

• Plant cells have large vacuoles for storage, while animal cells have smaller ones.

Further Insight:

• Animal Cell:

• Type: Eukaryotic cell, found in multicellular organisms.

• Cell Wall: Absent; has a flexible plasma membrane.

• Key Organelles:

○ Nucleus: Contains genetic material (DNA).

○ Mitochondria: Produces energy (ATP).

○ Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER): Involved in protein and lipid synthesis.

○ Golgi Apparatus: Packaging and transportation of proteins.

○ Lysosomes: Responsible for digestion and waste removal.

• Special Structures:

○ Centrioles: Play a role in cell division.

• Other Features: Lacks chloroplasts and a large central vacuole.

• Plant Cell:

• Type: Eukaryotic cell, found in plants.

• Cell Wall: Present; made of cellulose, providing structural strength.

• Key Organelles:

○ Nucleus: Contains genetic material (DNA).

○ Mitochondria: Produces energy (ATP).

○ Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER): Involved in protein and lipid synthesis.

○ Golgi Apparatus: Packaging and transportation of proteins.

○ Chloroplasts: Enable photosynthesis (conversion of light energy into chemical energy).

○ Large Central Vacuole: Maintains turgor pressure and stores nutrients.

• Other Features: Contains plasmodesmata (channels for communication between cells).

Key Differences:

• Chloroplasts: Present in plant cells, absent in animal cells.

• Cell Wall: Present in plant cells, absent in animal cells.

• Vacuole: Large central vacuole in plant cells; small or no vacuole in animal cells.

• Centrioles: Present in animal cells, typically absent in plant cells

questions.q_en:
Match the following cell organelles with their correct functions:

Column 1Column 2
i. Golgi apparatusa. ATP production
ii. Lysosomeb. Protein synthesis
iii. Mitochondrionc. Digestive enzymes for breakdown
iv. Ribosomed. Packaging and secretion of proteins

Select the correct match:
questions.solution_en:
• The Golgi apparatus is involved in modifying and packaging proteins for secretion.

• Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes responsible for breaking down waste materials.

• Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses of the cell," responsible for ATP production.

• Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

Further Insight:

Organelle NameFunction
MitochondriaKnown as the "powerhouse of the cell." They generate ATP through aerobic respiration. They contain their own DNA and ribosomes, allowing them to self-replicate.
RibosomesSites of protein synthesis. They translate mRNA to form specific polypeptides, functioning in the cytoplasm or on the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum.
Golgi ApparatusModifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles. Plays a role in the synthesis of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
Lysosomes"Suicide bags" of the cell; they digest foreign substances and worn-out organelles using hydrolytic enzymes. Can trigger autolysis in damaged cells.
NucleolusLocated within the nucleus, responsible for ribosome synthesis and assembly.
PlasmodesmataFound in plant cells, they are channels that allow communication and transport between adjacent plant cells.

questions.q_en:
Match the following organelles with their structural or functional descriptions:

Column 1Column 2
i. Peroxisomesa. Contains enzymes to break down fatty acids
ii. Nucleolusb. Produces ribosomal RNA (rRNA)
iii. Smooth ERc. Involved in lipid and steroid synthesis
iv. Microtubulesd. Provides shape and mechanical support to cells

Select the correct match:
questions.solution_en:
• Peroxisomes contain oxidative enzymes that detoxify alcohol and break down fatty acids.

• The nucleolus is located in the nucleus and produces rRNA, essential for ribosome assembly.

• The smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes lipids and steroids and detoxifies harmful metabolic byproducts.

• Microtubules are part of the cytoskeleton and help maintain the cell's shape and facilitate intracellular transport.

Further Insight:

Organelle NameFunction
Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)Rough ER: Synthesizes proteins, Smooth ER: Synthesizes lipids and detoxifies harmful substances in liver cells.
CytoskeletonProvides structural support, maintains cell shape, and assists in cell movement and intracellular transport. Composed of microtubules, actin filaments, etc.
ChloroplastsFound only in plant cells; the site of photosynthesis. Contain chlorophyll and have their own DNA and ribosomes, similar to mitochondria.
Plasma MembraneSemi-permeable membrane that controls the entry and exit of substances. Composed of a phospholipid bilayer, essential for maintaining homeostasis.
Cell WallFound only in plant cells, provides structural strength and rigidity. Made of cellulose, it protects cells from osmotic stress.
CentrosomesPlay a role in organizing microtubules and are crucial during cell division (mitosis). Contain centrioles in animal cells.
PeroxisomesBreak down fatty acids and detoxify harmful substances. Produce hydrogen peroxide as a byproduct, which is broken down by catalase.
Cilia and FlagellaCilia: Help in movement of materials across the cell surface; Flagella: Aid in cell motility (e.g., sperm cells).
NucleolusLocated within the nucleus, responsible for ribosome synthesis and assembly.
